newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Danieli, SMS, Pomini vie for Abu Dhabi steel deal.
newsitem.headline: Danieli, SMS, Pomini vie for Abu Dhabi steel deal.

text.p: Italy's Danieli and Pomini, and Germany's SMS Schloemann Siemag AG are in the running for a deal worth around $80 million to equip a steel plant in Abu Dhabi, the Emirates News reported on Wednesday.

The government-owned newspaper said Pomini had submitted the lowest bid at $72.48 million. It was followed by SMS Schloemann Siemag with a bid of $74.39 million and then Danieli, with a bid for $79.84 million.
Pomini SpA is part of Italy's Techint group. SMS Schloemann Siemag is a unit of MAN AG.

Earlier this week Issa Atiq, director general of Abu Dhabi's General Industry Corp (GIC), told Reuters the Abu Dhabi government would soon award the contract. He said the factory would produce 500,000 tonnes of steel bars a year.
"GIC will float another tender for the construction of buildings, estimated at $30 million once the contract for the supply of equipment is awarded," the Emirates News said.
It quoted a source close to the project as saying the privately-held Dubai Investment Co was likely to take a 30 percent stake in the plant.
Project consultants McLellan and Partners of Britain had submitted a plan for a possible second phase to increase the plant's annual capacity by another 500,000 tonnes, it added.
